Batch 5 manual enrichment — A Taxpayer v The Commissioners for HMRC

storyline.title: Sister's childcare crisis keeps six UK days out of residence count
storyline.summary: A taxpayer who relocated to Ireland before a large dividend relied on the statutory residence test's exceptional-circumstances rule for six days spent helping her alcoholic twin sister care for neglected children. HMRC denied the days; the Upper Tribunal agreed. The Court of Appeal restored the tribunal's fact-sensitive finding that the crisis was exceptional and prevented her leaving.

stages.title: Taxpayer moves to Ireland before tax year
stages.what_happened: She relocated to Dublin on 4 April 2015, just before 2015/16, while her husband remained in England.
stages.why_it_matters: Sought non-UK residence before receiving large dividends.

stages.title: Emergency visits to care for sister's children
stages.what_happened: In December 2015 and February 2016 she stayed six days in the UK stabilising her twin sister's dysfunctional household.
stages.why_it_matters: Days would exceed the 45-day limit unless excluded.

stages.title: First-tier Tribunal accepts exceptional circumstances
stages.what_happened: The FTT held the combination of alcoholism and care for minor children was exceptional under paragraph 22(4).
stages.why_it_matters: Excluded six crisis days from the residence count.

stages.title: Upper Tribunal reverses on prevention and exceptionality
stages.what_happened: The UT held moral obligations could not prevent departure and re-made the decision for HMRC.
stages.why_it_matters: Found the taxpayer UK resident for 2015/16.

stages.title: Court of Appeal restores FTT decision
stages.what_happened: Nugee LJ allowed the appeal on all grounds, restoring non-residence for 2015/16.

turning_points.label: Six days caring for sister's children
turning_points.impact: Determined UK residence for £8m dividend tax.

turning_points.label: Exceptional circumstances upheld
turning_points.impact: Confirmed moral/family crisis can count under SRT.

notes: Tax year and tribunal dates explicit.

Batch 5 manual enrichment — Hulley Enterprises Limited & Ors v The Russian Federation

storyline.title: Yukos enforcement: Dutch arbitration finding binds Russia in England
storyline.summary: Former Yukos shareholders enforcing multibillion-dollar treaty awards argued Russia could not reopen whether it agreed to arbitrate because Dutch courts had already decided the point. Russia said state immunity issues must always be determined afresh. The Court of Appeal agreed with the judge that issue estoppel applies, dismissing Russia's jurisdictional challenge.

parties.name: Hulley Enterprises Limited and other Yukos shareholders

stages.title: ECT tribunal awards over $50bn against Russia
stages.what_happened: In July 2014 the tribunal found Russia breached the Energy Charter Treaty and awarded massive damages to Yukos shareholders.
stages.why_it_matters: Created the underlying arbitral awards sought to be enforced.

stages.title: Claimants seek enforcement in England
stages.what_happened: In 2015 they commenced English enforcement proceedings under the Arbitration Act 1996.
stages.why_it_matters: Brought the dispute into the English courts.

stages.title: Hague Court of Appeal finds binding arbitration agreement
stages.what_happened: In February 2020 the Dutch court rejected Russia's no-agreement challenge and reinstated the awards.
stages.why_it_matters: Finally decided Russia had agreed to arbitrate.

stages.title: Cockerill J finds issue estoppel
stages.what_happened: On preliminary issues in November 2023 the judge held Russia was estopped from denying the arbitration agreement.
stages.why_it_matters: Prevented Russia reopening the arbitration-agreement issue.

stages.title: Court of Appeal dismisses Russia's appeal
stages.what_happened: Males LJ held issue estoppel applies to section 9 state immunity determinations.
stages.why_it_matters: Confirmed foreign judgment binds on immunity analysis.

turning_points.label: Dutch court confirms arbitration agreement
turning_points.impact: Provided the foreign judgment underpinning estoppel.

turning_points.label: Issue estoppel upheld on immunity
turning_points.impact: Barred Russia from relitigating jurisdiction in England.

notes: Major dates stated; some procedural dates approximate.

records.notes: Batch 5 manual enrichment — Kristie Higgs v Farmor's School

storyline.title: Christian school worker wins belief discrimination appeal
storyline.summary: A pastoral administrator posted Christian views about sex education on Facebook, was reported by a parent, and dismissed for gross misconduct. Employment tribunals rejected her discrimination claim and the EAT remitted the direct discrimination issue. Underhill LJ held the dismissal was because of protected belief and substituted a finding in her favour.

stages.title: Parent complains about Facebook posts
stages.what_happened: On 26 October 2018 a parent emailed the head teacher alleging homophobic posts about relationships education.

stages.title: School suspends and dismisses Mrs Higgs
stages.what_happened: After investigation she was summarily dismissed for gross misconduct in January 2019; internal appeal failed.
stages.why_it_matters: Ended her employment and led to tribunal proceedings.

stages.title: Employment tribunal rejects discrimination claims
stages.what_happened: In October 2020 the tribunal dismissed direct discrimination and harassment claims.
stages.why_it_matters: Forced appeal to the EAT on belief discrimination.

stages.title: EAT remits direct discrimination issue
stages.what_happened: The EAT remitted whether dismissal was unlawful direct discrimination, while rejecting other grounds.
stages.why_it_matters: Kept alive the core belief-discrimination claim.

stages.title: Court of Appeal substitutes success on direct discrimination
stages.what_happened: Underhill LJ allowed the appeal and held the dismissal was direct discrimination because of religion or belief.
stages.why_it_matters: Major victory on belief discrimination; other issues remitted if still needed.

turning_points.label: Social media posts reported
turning_points.impact: Started disciplinary process leading to dismissal.

turning_points.label: Direct discrimination finding substituted
turning_points.impact: Held dismissal was because of protected belief.

Batch 5 manual enrichment — Richard Hughes v HMRC & Anor

storyline.title: Tax scheme prosecution survivor loses civil claim
storyline.summary: Prosecuted over a share-loss-relief investment scheme, Richard Hughes saw criminal charges dismissed because the indictment was defective. He then sued HMRC and the CPS for malicious prosecution and misfeasance. The High Court granted summary judgment for the defendants, and the Court of Appeal refused permission to appeal.

parties.name: HMRC and the Crown Prosecution Service

stages.title: HMRC investigates ZP investment scheme
stages.what_happened: From 2010 HMRC investigated a scheme involving share loss relief on failed companies.
stages.why_it_matters: Identified Hughes as a suspect in the tax fraud investigation.

stages.title: Hughes charged with revenue cheating offences
stages.what_happened: Following counsel's advice he was charged by written requisition in December 2015.
stages.why_it_matters: Commenced the criminal proceedings later challenged.

stages.title: Crown Court dismisses charges
stages.what_happened: In May 2017 the judge held the indictment disclosed no offence known to law.
stages.why_it_matters: Ended prosecution but left civil remedies in issue.

stages.title: Hughes issues malicious prosecution proceedings
stages.what_happened: In December 2021 he commenced civil claims against HMRC and CPS, including assigned company rights.
stages.why_it_matters: Sought damages for the failed prosecution.

stages.title: Court refuses permission to appeal summary judgment
stages.what_happened: Davis and Baker LJJ refused permission, upholding Jay J's summary judgment for the defendants.

turning_points.label: Indictment dismissed as defective
turning_points.impact: Ended prosecution but did not prove malice.

turning_points.label: No real prospect on cause or malice
turning_points.impact: Blocked further civil recovery.

notes: Major dates from judgment; civil issue date approximate to month.

records.notes: Batch 5 manual enrichment — A v Disclosure and Barring Service

storyline.title: Barred list entry kept over possible junior football coaching
storyline.summary: A man with adult sexual offence convictions sought removal from the Children's Barred List so he could help at his son's football club. DBS kept him barred because he had completed FA coaching qualifications and might in future undertake regulated activity. The Upper Tribunal and Court of Appeal upheld the listing as lawful and proportionate.

stages.title: Convictions for sexual and violent offences
stages.what_happened: Between 2008 and 2011 he was convicted of offences against adult women, leading to SOPO and listing.
stages.why_it_matters: Provided the conduct underpinning barred-list inclusion.

stages.title: Included on Children's and Adult Barred Lists
stages.what_happened: He was placed on both barred lists; later removed from the Adult Barred List only.
stages.why_it_matters: Started safeguarding restrictions on regulated activity.

stages.title: DBS refuses removal from Children's Barred List
stages.what_happened: In January 2022 DBS found he might coach children's football and remained a safeguarding risk.
stages.why_it_matters: Maintained CBL entry despite adult-list removal.

stages.title: Upper Tribunal dismisses appeal
stages.what_happened: The UT upheld regulated-activity and proportionality findings in September 2023.
stages.why_it_matters: Rejected A's challenge to remaining on the CBL.

stages.title: Court of Appeal dismisses appeal
stages.what_happened: Macur LJ held no error in the UT's 'might in future' and proportionality analysis.

turning_points.label: DBS keeps CBL entry for coaching risk
turning_points.impact: Blocked voluntary work with children's football.

turning_points.label: Appeal on regulated activity fails
turning_points.impact: Listing remains; future review still possible.

notes: Anonymised judgment; some dates from UT recital.

records.notes: Batch 6 manual enrichment — Working on Wellbeing Ltd Trading as Optima Health v Secretary of State for Work and Pensions & Anor

storyline.title: Optima's overpriced line items and DWP's refusal to clarify
storyline.summary: Working on Wellbeing bid for a DWP workplace-health call-off but three line items exceeded framework caps, so DWP excluded the entire tender. Optima argued the ITT did not require automatic disqualification and that obvious errors should have been clarified. The Court of Appeal agreed and held DWP should have awarded the contract.

parties.name: Secretary of State for Work and Pensions

stages.title: DWP framework for workplace health services
stages.what_happened: DWP established a framework with maximum prices for call-off contracts including RWIND services.
stages.why_it_matters: Set the pricing ceiling that later triggered exclusion.

stages.title: Optima submits call-off tender
stages.what_happened: Optima bid for a call-off contract but three line items quoted above the framework maximum prices.
stages.why_it_matters: Created the pricing errors at the centre of the dispute.

stages.title: DWP excludes entire bid without clarification
stages.what_happened: DWP treated the overpriced items as mandatorily excluding the whole tender and did not seek clarification.
stages.why_it_matters: The decision challenged as irrational and disproportionate.

stages.title: High Court upholds DWP
stages.what_happened: At first instance the court rejected Optima's challenge to the exclusion decision.
stages.why_it_matters: Forced appeal on mandatory exclusion and clarification duty.

stages.title: Court of Appeal allows appeal
stages.what_happened: Coulson LJ held paragraph 2.2 was not mandatory, clarification was required, and Optima should have won.
stages.why_it_matters: Restores competitive outcome subject to remedy agreement.

turning_points.label: Whole bid excluded without clarification
turning_points.impact: Triggered judicial review and appeal.

turning_points.label: Mandatory exclusion rejected
turning_points.impact: Held DWP should have awarded Optima the contract.

notes: Core issues explicit; exact tender dates not individually stated in source.

Batch 6 manual enrichment — West Sussex County Council v AB & Anor

storyline.title: A DOLs-regulated teenager and an unnecessary care order
storyline.summary: A profoundly troubled 17-year-old remained at home under intensive DOLs supervision and an interim care order. Despite universal support for the care plan, the judge made a final care order to lock in local authority commitment. The Court of Appeal set it aside, holding that care orders cannot be used merely to galvanise statutory duties already accepted.

stages.title: DOLs orders authorise home care package
stages.what_happened: From July 2023 CD was subject to DOLs orders with 24-hour carers in her mother's home.
stages.why_it_matters: Established the intensive regulated framework later argued to make a care order unnecessary.

stages.title: Interim care order and threshold conceded
stages.what_happened: Care proceedings began in November 2023 on the ground CD was beyond parental control; threshold was accepted.
stages.why_it_matters: Introduced shared parental responsibility pending final hearing.

stages.title: Judge makes final care order
stages.what_happened: On 7 June 2024 the judge placed CD in the authority's care alongside continuing DOLs authorisation.

stages.title: Council and mother appeal on proportionality
stages.what_happened: Both appellants argued the care order added nothing to the existing DOLs-regulated package.
stages.why_it_matters: Raised Re JW and continuing High Court oversight.

stages.title: Care order set aside
stages.what_happened: McFarlane P allowed the appeal, holding the judge erred in using a care order to galvanise statutory duties.
stages.why_it_matters: CD remains under DOLs; care order discharged.

turning_points.label: Final care order made
turning_points.impact: Created the disproportionate interference under appeal.

turning_points.label: Galvanisation rationale rejected
turning_points.impact: Confirmed care orders cannot compel existing statutory duties.

records.notes: Batch 6 manual enrichment — Secretary of State for the Home Department v PG

storyline.title: A convicted gay Sri Lankan and the limits of country guidance
storyline.summary: PG, a gay Tamil convicted of sexual offences against boys, resisted deportation to Sri Lanka on Article 3 grounds. UT Judge Perkins allowed his appeal, finding post-guidance evidence showed prosecutions of gay men and that living discreetly would be oppressive. The Court of Appeal set aside the decision for inadequate analysis and remitted for rehearing.

parties.name: Secretary of State for the Home Department

stages.title: PG enters UK on student visa
stages.what_happened: A Sri Lankan Tamil entered the UK in January 2008 to study fashion design.
stages.why_it_matters: Establishes long residence before criminal and asylum history.

stages.title: Convicted of sexual offences against children
stages.what_happened: In 2012 PG was convicted of sexual activity with boys aged 13–15 and attempted rape, receiving four years.
stages.why_it_matters: Triggered foreign-criminal deportation liability and dangerousness presumption.

stages.title: Home Office grants discretionary leave
stages.what_happened: In 2013 the SSHD accepted PG could not live discreetly in Sri Lanka and granted six months' leave.
stages.why_it_matters: Prior acceptance of Article 3 risk later relied on by PG.

stages.title: UT allows appeal on Article 3
stages.what_happened: In June 2023 the UT allowed PG's appeal, departing partially from LH & IP on prosecutions.

stages.title: Court of Appeal remits for rehearing
stages.what_happened: Baker LJ allowed the SSHD's appeal for insufficient country guidance analysis and remitted to the UT.
stages.why_it_matters: Article 3 issue unresolved; deportation remains live.

turning_points.label: Discreet-living finding in 2013
turning_points.impact: Shaped PG's later Article 3 case.

turning_points.label: Inadequate UT reasoning
turning_points.impact: Set aside permissive deportation decision.

notes: Major dates stated in chronology; appeal hand-down date not in metadata.
